purpose: Adversarially audit only the frozen validated Codex result, waiver-aware comparison and synthesis plan without acquiring new research facts.
post_audit_holds: Claude and Grok absence remains visible and confidence remains medium.
The WM-SFT-004 parent signal has no relation-ledger edge and grants no composition, ownership, mutation, release or cascade authority.
Provider-specific registry lifecycle, model and data rights, license, IP, export, privacy, security, safety, jurisdiction and records profiles remain mandatory before adoption.
Registration, approval, publication, deployability, deployment and active operation remain separate assertions.
All catalog, registry, card, BOM, distribution, provenance, verification and lineage mappings remain release-pinned and loss-declaring.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 remains pinned while its announced revision is incomplete.
audit_findings: The registry boundary is coherent: the entry owns registration identity, discoverability and lifecycle assertions while model, training, evaluation and deployment masters remain external.
The structure prevents model family, version, immutable artifact, alias, model card, approval, publication and deployment from collapsing into one identity or state.
Digest, signature, provenance, rights, quality, safety and fitness claims remain independently evidenced.
Popularity and adoption are method-bound observations and do not imply quality, approval or safe use.
Autonomous approval, publication, signature, revocation, access expansion, disclosure, deployment and destructive cleanup are explicitly prohibited without delegated authority.
No unresolved critical semantic conflict prevents reviewable-draft publication.
